messages:
maya: Quick sync — customer 'AtlasSearch' reported rerank flakiness after we rolled a new embedding variant. Symptoms: rerank scores jumpy, some queries return empties. Need a short PRD + playbook for dimension mismatches, normalization choices, and batch semantics. Can we triage and lock a minimal ship scope?

liam: Do we have logs or a repro? saw this once in staging when a model quant change changed embed dim. sample error from the reranker: `InvalidEmbeddingShape: expected 768 got 512`

sarah: I started a one-page PRD draft in drive (will paste summary here). Proposed scope: 1) detection & strict reject path + clear error code, 2) optional automatic projection + policy, 3) normalization policy consistent across indexing & serving, 4) migration playbook for customers + reindex estimator. Acceptance criteria (first pass):
- System returns clear 4xx on dim mismatch when `compat=reject`
- `compat=project` must keep cosine equivalence within 1e-3 ndcg on a provided eval set
- No silent reprioritization: batch order preserved and KV-cache unaffected
- Canary run (1% traffic, 48h) with NDGC delta < 2% and p95 latency delta < 10ms

raj: Edgecases to call out:
- Mixed-index: older vectors (512d) coexisting with new (768d) in nearest-neighbor indexes -> query-time mixing
- Normalization drift: some pipelines use L2, others unit-sphere by default -> ranking differences depending on dot vs cosine
- Batch semantics: padding/truncation can change effective vector if we use grouped pooling or fused ops
- Determinism: tokenization/seed differences upstream can create spurious dim changes in rare cases

emily: QA checklist:
- Synthetic test harness that emits index with N vectors at dims {512,768,1024} and runs cross-dim queries, measure fallback correctness
- Evaluate both `normalize=true` and `normalize=false` for dot vs cosine routing
- Regression tests: stored replay of customer query set to compute ndcg pre/post migration
- Load test: ensure batching behavior stable when requests contain mixed-dim payloads (use the batcher + KV cache sim)

ops-bot: deploy:canary started for `rerank-compat-v1` — 1% traffic.

sarah: Refining acceptance criteria (more concrete):
- Functional: `400 EMB_DIM_MISMATCH` returned within 200ms for rejected requests
- Compatibility: when `on_mismatch=project`, average ndcg drop <= 0.01 on the curated eval set, 95% of queries within tolerance
- Performance: p95 latency increase <= 12ms for rerank path vs baseline
- Observability: per-request metadata includes `original_dim`, `served_dim`, `compat_action`, and audit log entry for any automated projection
- Operational: reindex estimation script produces cost and time estimate within 20% of actual for sample workloads

liam: What's the migration cost ballpark? reindexing 1M vectors from 512->768 with our internal tooling on a 4-GPU pool — rough numbers?

maya: Quick calc: projection (cheap) vs full re-embed (expensive). For full re-embed we estimate ~2 GPU-hours per 100k vectors on our bench -> ~20 GPU-hours for 1M. Ops + SRE to schedule. Projection (learned linear map) is CPU cheap: <30m for 1M if using batched matmul and streaming.

raj: I'll open an RFC with tests + a tiny CLI tool `rwd-embed-compat` for local dry-run. Draft config snippet: ```
embed_compat:
  on_mismatch: reject | project | allow_mixed
  projection_mode: linear | pad_zero | truncate
  normalize: l2 | none
  batch_padding: pad | fail
  telemetry: emit_metrics
```

emily: Canary notes: if we see NDGC drift > 2% we auto-roll back. Also add a smoke that checks index mixing doesn't return vectors from incompatible dims (should return explicit error code instead).

maya: Decision for now (minimal ship):
1) Implement strict `reject` by default with descriptive error and remediation hint.
2) Implement `project` as opt-in with carefully validated projection matrices + eval harness.
3) Add `normalize=l2` as recommended default in SDK + server side toggle.
4) Provide reindex estimator + migration runbook.
5) Hook observability (per-request fields + ndcg guardrails) and canary policy (1% -> 10% -> 100% with rollback triggers).

liam: 👍. I'll own runtime changes + perf bench. raj take RFC + CLI. emily please own QA harness and regression suite. sarah can you finalize PRD with acceptance criteria and launch checklist?

sarah: on it, will circulate draft within 24h and tag eng-infra and support for migration SLAs.

maya: Thanks all. Tagging @support and @sales for the customer comms draft after we have the runbook. We'll sync tomorrow 10:00 to lock timeline.
